2:117.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَإِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
2:117.en: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! When He decreeth a thing, He saith unto it only: Be! and it is

6:101.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ صَٰحِبَةࣱۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
6:101.en: The Originator of the heavens and the earth! How can He have a child, when there is for Him no consort, when He created all things and is Aware of all things

13:1.ar: الٓمٓرۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِۗ وَٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
13:1.en: Alif. Lam. Mim. Ra. These are verses of the Scripture. That which is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the Truth, but most of mankind believe not

13:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّكُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ
13:2.en: Allah it is Who raised up the heavens without visible supports, then mounted the Throne, and compelled the sun and the moon to be of service, each runneth unto an appointed term; He ordereth the course; He detaileth the revelations, that haply ye may be certain of the meeting with your Lord

13:3.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣰ اۖ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
13:3.en: And He it is Who spread out the earth and placed therein firm hills and flowing streams, and of all fruits He placed therein two spouses (male and female). He covereth the night with the day. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought

13:4.ar: وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قِطَعࣱ مُّتَجَٰوِرَٰتࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣱ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَزَرۡعࣱ وَنَخِيلࣱ صِنۡوَانࣱ وَغَيۡرُ صِنۡوَانࣲ يُسۡقَىٰ بِمَآءࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعۡضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فِي ٱلۡأُكُلِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
13:4.en: And in the Earth are neighbouring tracts, vineyards and ploughed lands, and date-palms, like and unlike, which are watered with one water. And we have made some of them to excel others in fruit. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who have sense

25:45.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنࣰ ا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلࣰ ا
25:45.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread the shade - And if He willed He could have made it still - then We have made the sun its pilot

25:46.ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡنَا قَبۡضࣰ ا يَسِيرࣰ ا
25:46.en: Then We withdraw it unto Us, a gradual withdrawal

25:47.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ لِبَاسࣰ ا وَٱلنَّوۡمَ سُبَاتࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورࣰ ا
25:47.en: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection

25:48.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشۡرَۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ طَهُورࣰ ا
25:48.en: And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy, and We send down purifying water from the sky

25:49.ar: لِّنُحۡـِۧيَ بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ ا وَنُسۡقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقۡنَآ أَنۡعَٰمࣰ ا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:49.en: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof

25:53.ar: ۞وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَرَجَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَيۡنِ هَٰذَا عَذۡبࣱ فُرَاتࣱ وَهَٰذَا مِلۡحٌ أُجَاجࣱ وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَهُمَا بَرۡزَخࣰ ا وَحِجۡرࣰ ا مَّحۡجُورࣰ ا
25:53.en: And He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and hath set a bar and a forbidding ban between them

25:54.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ بَشَرࣰ ا فَجَعَلَهُۥ نَسَبࣰ ا وَصِهۡرࣰ اۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرࣰ ا
25:54.en: And He it is Who hath created man from water, and hath appointed for him kindred by blood and kindred by marriage; for thy Lord is ever Powerful

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, and therewith We bring forth buds of every kind; We bring forth the green blade from which We bring forth the thick-clustered grain; and from the date-palm, from the pollen thereof, spring pendant bunches; and (We bring forth) gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, alike and unlike. Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who believe

16:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:3.en: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. High be He Exalted above all that they associate (with Him)

16:4.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
16:4.en: He hath created man from a drop of fluid, yet behold! he is an open opponent

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And wherein is beauty for you, when ye bring them home, and when ye take them out to pasture

16:7.ar: وَتَحۡمِلُ أَثۡقَالَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلۡأَنفُسِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:7.en: And they bear your loads for you unto a land ye could not reach save with great trouble to yourselves. Lo! your Lord is Full of Pity, Merciful

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:8.en: And horses and mules and asses (hath He created) that ye may ride them, and for ornament. And He createth that which ye know not

16:9.ar: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرࣱۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
16:9.en: And Allah's is the direction of the way, and some (roads) go not straight. And had He willed He would have led you all aright

16:10.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰۖ لَّكُم مِّنۡهُ شَرَابࣱ وَمِنۡهُ شَجَرࣱ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
16:10.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, whence ye have drink, and whence are trees on which ye send your beasts to pasture

16:11.ar: يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرۡعَ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:11.en: Therewith He causeth crops to grow for you, and the olive and the date-palm and grapes and all kinds of fruit. Lo! herein is indeed a portent for people who reflect

16:12.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ وَٱلنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَٰتُۢ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
16:12.en: And He hath constrained the night and the day and the sun and the moon to be of service unto you, and the stars are made subservient by His command. Lo! herein indeed are portents for people who have sense

16:18.ar: وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:18.en: And if ye would count the favour of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! Allah is indeed Forgiving, Merciful

Nb0ZZkd5Kqo.speaker_note: Glorious Names of Allah series, single voice, recalls his own childhood in a village
Nb0ZZkd5Kqo.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Inventive One, Al-Badi'
Nb0ZZkd5Kqo.one_line: Al-Badi': Allah created without any prior model, His creation is beautiful in every detail, and we should notice it and be creative ourselves.
Nb0ZZkd5Kqo.summary: He defines Al-Badi' as the One who brought creation into being with no earlier example, in a way that is beautiful and breathtaking. The name appears only twice in the Quran, both times about the heavens and earth, yet its meaning runs through whole passages. He contrasts human invention, which always imitates something already there, such as planes copying birds and submarines copying sea creatures, with Allah's creation, which copies nothing. He then reads long passages from Ar-Ra'd, Al-Furqan, Al-An'am and An-Nahl about the sky raised without pillars, one water producing endless flavours, shadows, sleep, rain, two seas, livestock, the stars and the sea, asking whether the One who creates is like one who cannot. He argues that modern life has numbed us to this beauty, pointing to videos of colourblind people seeing colour and deaf children hearing for the first time, and to his childhood nights on a village rooftop staring at the sky. He cites the hadith of a man who called on Allah as Badi' al-Samawat, which some scholars took as the greatest name. He closes by urging people to be creative and innovative in life and in how they engage the Quran, while not inventing acts of worship, and to appreciate the small beauties of creation.

outline.heading: Meaning of Al-Badi' and its two occurrences
outline.gist: The One who produced creation with no earlier example, beautifully; the name appears twice, both about the heavens and earth, one rejecting the claim that He has a son.

outline.heading: Human invention copies, Allah's does not
outline.gist: Planes, helicopters and submarines imitate birds, insects and sea creatures; everything Allah made has no prior model.

outline.heading: We rarely think of Allah as the Most Creative
outline.gist: We dwell on His knowledge and power but forget His creativity, though whole passages of the Quran describe it.

outline.heading: Sky without pillars, sun, moon and the spread earth
outline.gist: Ar-Ra'd describes the heavens raised without visible supports, the sun and moon running, and the earth with mountains, rivers and paired plants.

outline.heading: One water, countless flavours
outline.gist: Neighbouring plots, vines and palms are watered by the same water yet differ in taste and colour, a sign for those who think.

outline.heading: Shadows, sleep and rain
outline.gist: Al-Furqan points to stretched shadows, night for rest, day for rising, and winds that bring rain to revive dead land.

outline.heading: Two seas, human kinship and the variety of fruit
outline.gist: Sweet and salt seas kept apart, humans made from water and bound by lineage and marriage, and Al-An'am's crops, olives and pomegranates alike and unlike.

outline.heading: Livestock and riding animals
outline.gist: An-Nahl: man from a drop who becomes an arguer, cattle for warmth, food and beauty, and horses, mules and donkeys to ride and admire.

outline.heading: Rain, the sky and the sea in service of man
outline.gist: Rain, crops, the subjected night, day, sun, moon and stars, the sea with its fresh meat and pearls, and mountains, rivers and stars for finding the way.

outline.heading: Is the one who creates like one who cannot
outline.gist: His blessings and inventions are countless and filled with beauty.

outline.heading: Seeing colour and hearing for the first time
outline.gist: Videos of colourblind adults weeping at the sky and deaf children hearing a parent show how numb we have become to the beauty around us.

outline.heading: Village rooftop nights and beauty in detail
outline.gist: As a child during power cuts he lay on the roof watching the sky; the deeper you study creation, down to each cell, the more beauty you find.

outline.heading: You never tire of His creation
outline.gist: Beauty unfolds from what He placed in creation's beginning; human work bores us but people return each year to the same view, a sand grain or a snowflake.

outline.heading: Hadith of the greatest name
outline.gist: A man prayed calling on Allah as Badi' al-Samawat wal-Ard and the Prophet said he had asked by the greatest name; some scholars took this as that name.

outline.heading: Living the name: be creative, but not in inventing worship
outline.gist: Be innovative in life and in how you understand the Quran within its guidelines, never invent new acts of worship, and learn to appreciate small beauties.

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

6:102.ar: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَٱعۡبُدُوهُۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَكِيلࣱ‏
6:102.en: Such is Allah, your Lord. There is no Allah save Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He taketh care of all things

13:16.ar: قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ اۚ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ أَمۡ هَلۡ تَسۡتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتُ وَٱلنُّورُۗ أَمۡ جَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلۡقِهِۦ فَتَشَٰبَهَ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّٰرُ
13:16.en: Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt? Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty

7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

4:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةࣲ وَخَلَقَ مِنۡهَا زَوۡجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنۡهُمَا رِجَالࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا وَنِسَآءࣰۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡحَامَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ رَقِيبࣰ ا
4:1.en: O mankind! Be careful of your duty to your Lord Who created you from a single soul and from it created its mate and from them twain hath spread abroad a multitude of men and women. Be careful of your duty toward Allah in Whom ye claim (your rights) of one another, and toward the wombs (that bare you). Lo! Allah hath been a watcher over you

31:10.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةࣲۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجࣲ كَرِيمٍ
31:10.en: He hath created the heavens without supports that ye can see, and hath cast into the earth firm hills, so that it quake not with you; and He hath dispersed therein all kinds of beasts. And We send down water from the sky and We cause (plants) of every goodly kind to grow therein

31:11.ar: هَٰذَا خَلۡقُ ٱللَّهِ فَأَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦۚ بَلِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
31:11.en: This is the Creation of Allah. Now show me that which those (ye worship) beside Him have created. Nay, but the wrong-doers are in error manifest

23:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن سُلَٰلَةࣲ مِّن طِينࣲ‏
23:12.en: Verily We created man from a product of wet earth

23:13.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ نُطۡفَةࣰ فِي قَرَارࣲ مَّكِينࣲ‏
23:13.en: Then placed him as a drop (of seed) in a safe lodging

23:14.ar: ثُمَّ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلنُّطۡفَةَ عَلَقَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡعَلَقَةَ مُضۡغَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمُضۡغَةَ عِظَٰمࣰ ا فَكَسَوۡنَا ٱلۡعِظَٰمَ لَحۡمࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَٰهُ خَلۡقًا ءَاخَرَۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقِينَ
23:14.en: Then fashioned We the drop a clot, then fashioned We the clot a little lump, then fashioned We the little lump bones, then clothed the bones with flesh, and then produced it as another creation. So blessed be Allah, the Best of creators

32:7.ar: ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينࣲ‏
32:7.en: Who made all things good which He created, and He began the creation of man from clay

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, and therewith We bring forth buds of every kind; We bring forth the green blade from which We bring forth the thick-clustered grain; and from the date-palm, from the pollen thereof, spring pendant bunches; and (We bring forth) gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, alike and unlike. Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who believe

71:14.en: When He created you by (divers) stages

71:15.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ كَيۡفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ ا
71:15.en: See ye not how Allah hath created seven heavens in harmony

71:16.ar: وَجَعَلَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ سِرَاجࣰ ا
71:16.en: And hath made the moon a light therein, and made the sun a lamp

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth

71:18.ar: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمۡ فِيهَا وَيُخۡرِجُكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجࣰ ا
71:18.en: And afterward He maketh you return thereto, and He will bring you forth again, a (new) forthbringing

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say (O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see how He originated creation, then Allah bringeth forth the later growth. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

76:1.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ حِينࣱ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهۡرِ لَمۡ يَكُن شَيۡـࣰٔ ا مَّذۡكُورًا
76:1.en: Hath there come upon man (ever) any period of time in which he was a thing unremembered

41:9.ar: ۞قُلۡ أَئِنَّكُمۡ لَتَكۡفُرُونَ بِٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ وَتَجۡعَلُونَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
41:9.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the idolaters): Disbelieve ye verily in Him Who created the earth in two Days, and ascribe ye unto Him rivals? He (and none else) is the Lord of the Worlds

41:10.ar: وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ مِن فَوۡقِهَا وَبَٰرَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقۡوَٰتَهَا فِيٓ أَرۡبَعَةِ أَيَّامࣲ سَوَآءࣰ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
41:10.en: He placed therein firm hills rising above it, and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four Days, alike for (all) who ask

41:11.ar: ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانࣱ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلۡأَرۡضِ ٱئۡتِيَا طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا قَالَتَآ أَتَيۡنَا طَآئِعِينَ
41:11.en: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient

41:12.ar: فَقَضَىٰهُنَّ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَاتࣲ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ وَأَوۡحَىٰ فِي كُلِّ سَمَآءٍ أَمۡرَهَاۚ وَزَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَحِفۡظࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
41:12.en: Then He ordained them seven heavens in two Days and inspired in each heaven its mandate; and We decked the nether heaven with lamps, and rendered it inviolable. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Knower

57:3.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡأَوَّلُ وَٱلۡأٓخِرُ وَٱلظَّٰهِرُ وَٱلۡبَاطِنُۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
57:3.en: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things

38:75.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسۡجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقۡتُ بِيَدَيَّۖ أَسۡتَكۡبَرۡتَ أَمۡ كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَالِينَ
38:75.en: He said: O Iblis! What hindereth thee from falling prostrate before that which I have created with both My hands? Art thou too proud or art thou of the high exalted

16:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:3.en: He hath created the heavens and the earth with truth. High be He Exalted above all that they associate (with Him)

16:4.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
16:4.en: He hath created man from a drop of fluid, yet behold! he is an open opponent

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the cattle hath He created, whence ye have warm clothing and uses, and whereof ye eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And wherein is beauty for you, when ye bring them home, and when ye take them out to pasture

16:7.ar: وَتَحۡمِلُ أَثۡقَالَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلۡأَنفُسِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:7.en: And they bear your loads for you unto a land ye could not reach save with great trouble to yourselves. Lo! your Lord is Full of Pity, Merciful

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:8.en: And horses and mules and asses (hath He created) that ye may ride them, and for ornament. And He createth that which ye know not

zEJV_lUz2c0.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Khaliq, the Creator
zEJV_lUz2c0.one_line: Al-Khaliq with Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir: creation from nothing, life and purpose, why science deepens faith, and how we can create good.
zEJV_lUz2c0.summary: He presents Al-Khaliq alongside Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir, names that come together in the Quran. Khalq means bringing something into being where there was nothing, and also transforming a thing so deeply that before and after cannot be compared. He reads a chain of verses on creation: the heavens and earth in six days, humanity from one soul, the stages of the embryo, fruit ripening, the heavens in layers, and the challenge to show what anything else has created. Creation begins and ends with Allah alone, and the laws of physics are His. He then argues that science will never answer three questions: where existence came from, how matter first became alive, and why living things strive to survive and prosper, which he links to the names of the Creator, the Giver of life and the Giver of form and purpose. Allah did not need billions of years; time and space are His creations, and gradualness is our nature, not His. He warns against losing faith as science uncovers how creation unfolded and against rejecting the Big Bang or evolution on religious grounds, since a single cell programmed to produce all life is more awe-inspiring. Our share of the name is to transform neglected resources into services that create good for others.

outline.heading: Opening
Three names that come together
outline.gist: Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir appear together, and the verb of creating occurs countless times in the Quran.

outline.heading: Two meanings of khalq
outline.gist: Producing something where there was nothing, and transforming one form into another beyond comparison.

outline.heading: Creator of everything, owner of creation and command
outline.gist: Verses on Allah creating all things, the challenge of false partners, and the heavens and earth in six days.

outline.heading: Show me what others have created
outline.gist: Humanity from one soul and the sky without pillars; this is Allah's creation, so what have others made?

outline.heading: Stages of the embryo
outline.gist: From an extract of earth to a drop, a clot and flesh, then an entirely new creation; blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

outline.heading: Creation in sequence and stages
outline.gist: He perfected all He made, ripening fruit, layered heavens, humans grown from the earth like plants; walk the earth and see how creation began.

outline.heading: There was Allah and nothing else
outline.gist: There was a time humanity was not even a thought; the Prophet told the Yemenis there was only Allah.

outline.heading: Existence begins and ends with Allah alone
outline.gist: Our existence is a brief interval, and every law of nature from gravity to electromagnetism is His creation.

outline.heading: First mystery: existence from nothing
outline.gist: Science studies the universe after the Big Bang but not where the first matter and energy came from.

outline.heading: Second mystery: the first spark of life
outline.gist: How lifeless elements became a breathing organism is unknown; Allah is the one who grants life.

outline.heading: Third mystery: the drive to live and purpose
outline.gist: Science describes but cannot explain why living things strive to survive and prosper; Allah grants form and purpose.

outline.heading: Why did He create?
outline.gist: The question as old as humanity looking up at the stars.

outline.heading: Six days and billions of years
outline.gist: Allah did not need the time; we needed it to come forth in a universe of time and space.

outline.heading: First and Last: beyond time and space
outline.gist: Only One untouched by time and space can be both First and Last, Manifest and Hidden.

outline.heading: 'Created with My hands': you were meant to be here
outline.gist: Not literal hands but a sign that humanity was intended and close to Him, not a by-product.

outline.heading: Animals created for benefit and beauty
outline.gist: Livestock, horses and mules serve us and are beautiful, and He creates what we do not yet know.

outline.heading: Science should increase awe, not doubt
outline.gist: Losing faith on barely understanding how creation happened is arrogance; one cell programmed to produce all life is more awe-inspiring.

outline.heading: Do not fear science
outline.gist: The Quran gives broad strokes, not scientific detail, so it cannot contradict science; do not reject theories on religious grounds.

outline.heading: Gradualness is our nature, not His
outline.gist: Whether a millisecond or billions of years makes no difference to Allah; we live, learn and grow through time.

outline.heading: Living the name: create good
outline.gist: We cannot create from nothing, but we can transform neglected resources into services and opportunities for others.

outline.heading: Read texts with openness
outline.gist: Science will only strengthen faith; reread texts more figuratively where needed.

outline.heading: Outro

10:31.ar: قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَمَّن يَمۡلِكُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَمَن يُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَيُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَيِّ وَمَن يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَۚ فَسَيَقُولُونَ ٱللَّهُۚ فَقُلۡ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ
10:31.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Who provideth for you from the sky and the earth, or Who owneth hearing and sight; and Who bringeth forth the living from the dead and bringeth forth the dead from the living; and Who directeth the course? They will say: Allah. Then say: Will ye not then keep your duty (unto Him)

59:23.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ

67:1.ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
67:1.en: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things

2:107.ar: أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ

16:73.ar: وَيَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ رِزۡقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ

34:22.ar: قُلِ ٱدۡعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا لَهُمۡ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرۡكࣲ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡهُم مِّن ظَهِيرࣲ‏

He created you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in a threefold gloom. Such is Allah, your Lord. His is the Sovereignty. There is no Allah save Him. How then are ye turned away

WbhQgeZNP28.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The King of Kings, Al-Malik
WbhQgeZNP28.one_line: Al-Malik: Allah both rules and owns everything, so we use His possessions humbly and in ways He approves of.
WbhQgeZNP28.summary: He walks through the forms this name takes in the Quran: Al-Malik, Malik al-Mulk (Owner of all sovereignty), Maliki Yawm al-Din from Al-Fatihah, and Maleek, an intensive form. He draws a distinction between a ruler who may not own and an owner who may not rule, and argues Allah combines both. He then surveys the Quranic thread on sovereignty: Surat al-Mulk, the closing surah naming Allah King of mankind, the repeated statement that the heavens and earth belong to Him, and the long list of verses saying false gods own nothing, not even the film on a date stone or the weight of an atom. He shows how people who were given a little sovereignty misused it, Nimrod arguing with Ibrahim and Pharaoh boasting of Egypt, and how Iblis tempted Adam with an everlasting kingdom. He describes the Day of Judgment when Allah asks who the King is today and answers Himself, the vast kingdom shown to the people of Paradise, and the hadith of Allah folding the heavens and calling out to the tyrants. He ends by asking the audience to see that their house, body and soul are Allah's property, to behave with humility, and to use everything only as its Owner would approve, knowing they will be asked about it.

outline.heading: Forms of the name in the Quran
outline.gist: Al-Malik appears five times, alongside Malik al-Mulk, Maliki Yawm al-Din in Al-Fatihah, and the intensive Maleek, each meaning undisputed authority to command and forbid.

outline.heading: Ruling versus owning
outline.gist: A king may rule without owning and an owner may own without ruling; Allah's names cover both, and He is also Owner of kings.

outline.heading: Who owns your senses; Surat al-Mulk
outline.gist: Allah asks who owns hearing and sight, names Himself the King, the Holy, and opens Surat al-Mulk with sovereignty in His hand.

outline.heading: King of mankind and dominion of the heavens and earth
outline.gist: The last surah frames our relationship with Allah as Lord, King and God of people; over fifteen verses state the dominion of the heavens and earth is His.

outline.heading: False gods own nothing
outline.gist: Verses list what idols do not own: harm, benefit, life, death, resurrection, provision, the film on a date stone, an atom's weight, intercession or speech.

outline.heading: Owner of sovereignty gives and takes it
outline.gist: The dua in Aal-Imran: Allah grants and removes kingship and honour as He wills, and all good is in His hand.

outline.heading: Sovereignty granted to people
outline.gist: Nimrod argued with Ibrahim because of a small kingdom on loan from Allah; Allah gave Dawud kingship and wisdom and gave the family of Ibrahim a great kingdom.

outline.heading: Iblis's offer to Adam and Pharaoh's boast
outline.gist: Iblis tempted Adam with an everlasting kingdom and Adam learned that sovereignty is Allah's; Pharaoh boasted of Egypt's rivers and drowned beneath water.

outline.heading: Whose is the kingdom today
outline.gist: On the Day of Meeting Allah asks who rules today, answers Himself, and judges every soul fairly while the hearts of the oppressors rise to their throats.

outline.heading: The great kingdom of Paradise
outline.gist: In Jannah the believer looks around and sees bliss and an immense kingdom, as Ibrahim was shown the dominion of the heavens.

outline.heading: Hadith of folding the heavens
outline.gist: Allah folds the heavens and earth and calls out, I am the King, where are the tyrants and the arrogant; he stresses the language is figurative.

outline.heading: The King descends in the last third of the night
outline.gist: Allah calls out as the King asking who will pray, ask and seek forgiveness so He can answer them until dawn.

outline.heading: Living with the name: the King who created you
outline.gist: Living with Al-Malik starts with understanding the relationship: He created us from one soul and formed us in the darkness of the womb.

outline.heading: Everything you use belongs to Him
outline.gist: House, land, water, air, body and soul are Allah's possessions; understanding this calms us and makes us humble.

outline.heading: Use His property as He approves
outline.gist: If we use what is His we must use it in ways He accepts, because He will ask what we did with it; this is why His servants walk humbly on the earth.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Explains Al-Malik, Malik al-Mulk and Maleek, and the difference between ruling and owning.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: False objects of worship own nothing at all, so worship belongs to the one who owns everything.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Those given a little power, like Nimrod and Pharaoh, grew arrogant; knowing all is Allah's should make us humble.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: On the Day of Judgment Allah alone claims the kingdom, and Paradise reveals a great kingdom.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: We will be asked how we used the food, water, air and earth that belonged to Allah.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: The King descends at night offering to answer, give and forgive.

3:129.en: Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. He forgiveth whom He will, and punisheth whom He will. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

8:70.en: O Prophet! Say unto those captives who are in your hands: If Allah knoweth any good in your hearts He will give you better than that which hath been taken from you, and will forgive you. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا

3cpOAyzlcFE.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Ghafur, the Most Forgiving
3cpOAyzlcFE.one_line: Al-Ghafur: Allah's love to conceal and forgive, why sinning is inevitable, and four ways to live by this name in Ramadan.
3cpOAyzlcFE.summary: Speaking in mid-Ramadan, when forgiveness is the main goal, he notes that the three Arabic forms of the name appear in the Quran in numbers that match the kinds of sinners they address. Maghfirah means to cover and protect: Allah conceals faults in this life, covers them on the Day of Judgment and shields from punishment. He reads the verse that Allah forgives everything except shirk as deeply hopeful, since Allah asks for only one essential thing, and notes that prophets like Ibrahim and Isa pleaded for forgiveness even for those who rejected them. A wave of verses and hadith follow: the servant who sins repeatedly and is forgiven each time he asks, sins as high as the sky, the Prophet seeking forgiveness a hundred times a day. Sin is inevitable; the closer one draws to Allah, the more small sins one notices, and istighfar becomes a constructive habit of correcting oneself that builds people and societies. Allah judges forgiven believers privately and even turns sins into good deeds, while those who expose others will be exposed. He gives four applications: forgive others, as Abu Bakr was told to keep supporting the relative who slandered Aisha; conceal people's faults; bring a big good deed; and seek forgiveness abundantly and attentively.

outline.heading: Opening
Three forms of the name and their frequency
outline.gist: Ghafur, Ghaffar and Ghafir appear in numbers that match those who sin once, sin heavily, or sin repeatedly.

outline.heading: Maghfirah means to cover and protect
outline.gist: Allah conceals faults in this life, covers them on the Day of Judgment and preserves one from punishment.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's hope for forgiveness
outline.gist: Ibrahim hopes his Lord will forgive him on the Day of Judgment; Allah forgives whom He wills.

outline.heading: Everything forgiven except shirk: a hopeful verse
outline.gist: Allah asks only one bare minimum, to come without associating partners, and may forgive everything else.

outline.heading: Prophets plead even for those who rejected them
outline.gist: Isa and Ibrahim leave room for Allah's forgiveness, knowing how He loves to forgive; none can question Him.

outline.heading: Forgoing a threatened punishment is generosity
outline.gist: Breaking a promised reward is a flaw, but forgiving a threatened punishment is not.

outline.heading: Forgiveness offered to enemies and captives
outline.gist: Disbelievers who stop fighting are forgiven their past, and captives with good in their hearts are promised more than they lost.

outline.heading: The unified message of the prophets
outline.gist: Every prophet told his people that Allah calls them so He may forgive them.

outline.heading: The servant who keeps returning
outline.gist: A servant sins and asks forgiveness again and again, and Allah forgives him each time he asks.

outline.heading: Sins as high as the sky
outline.gist: Allah forgives whatever the amount for whoever calls on Him without shirk; constant istighfar brings a way out of every difficulty.

outline.heading: Sin is inevitable; seeking forgiveness is the point
outline.gist: The Prophet sought forgiveness a hundred times daily, and Allah would replace a sinless people with ones who sin and repent.

outline.heading: Closer to Allah, more sins noticed
outline.gist: Nearness reveals countless small faults; istighfar is a constructive mindset of correction that builds individuals and civilisations.

outline.heading: Nuh: seek forgiveness and blessings follow
outline.gist: Rain, wealth, children and gardens come as the natural outcome of sincere istighfar joined with intent to change.

outline.heading: Do not despair of Allah's mercy
outline.gist: Allah forgives all sins for those who have wronged themselves.

outline.heading: The private reckoning and sins turned to good deeds
outline.gist: Allah questions the forgiven believer behind a curtain, forgives what He concealed, and even turns his sins into good deeds.

outline.heading: Those who expose sins will be exposed
outline.gist: The ummah is forgiven except those who publicise sins; whoever exposes others will be exposed on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: First application: forgive others
outline.gist: Forgiving is among the hardest acts, but we cannot hope for Allah's total forgiveness without it.

outline.heading: Forgive even those who reject the Last Day
outline.gist: Believers are told to pardon disbelievers and leave accountability to Allah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr and the relative who slandered Aisha
outline.gist: Abu Bakr cut support to a poor relative who joined the slander, until the verse asking 'do you not love that Allah forgive you' moved him to restore it.

outline.heading: Resolve old grudges in these nights
outline.gist: Look back at unresolved conflicts and forgive, if you hope Allah will forgive your years of shortcomings.

outline.heading: Second application: conceal people's faults
outline.gist: Whoever covers a Muslim's fault, Allah covers his on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Third application: bring a big good deed
outline.gist: Good deeds erase bad ones; Uthman's funding of the Tabuk army in a hard year earned the Prophet's assurance.

outline.heading: Fourth application: abundant, attentive istighfar
outline.gist: Seek forgiveness while reflecting on specific sins; the Prophet's sensitive spirit saw faults we would count as good deeds.

8:72.en: Lo! those who believed and left their homes and strove with their wealth and their lives for the cause of Allah, and those who took them in and helped them: these are protecting friends one of another. Allah is Seer of what ye do

PTMAg6jpSsM.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment: Advocacy
PTMAg6jpSsM.one_line: Nusrah as advocacy: Muslims who have a voice in Canada are obligated to stand up for the oppressed, through media, lobbying and awareness.
PTMAg6jpSsM.summary: The fourth category in his series is advocacy, which he presents as the meaning of nusrah. When it comes from Allah the word means granting victory, but from people it means standing by, supporting and investing time, wealth and influence in a cause; he reads the verse on Allah aiding the Prophet on the night of Hijrah and the closing verses of Al-Anfal on believers as allies who must help those who seek aid. Hadith reinforce it: a Muslim never abandons his brother, supports him whether oppressed or oppressor by restraining him, and whoever watches someone humiliated without helping will be humiliated on Judgment Day. The Prophet never grew angry for himself but marched an army for allies massacred in breach of a treaty. Most here fled voicelessness, so a voice now is an obligation. Standing for others feels risky, but silence lets a wheel of oppression roll on until it crushes you; he recalls a Syrian colleague whose whole village was gassed. In the second khutbah he names media presence, organized lobbying rather than parties, keeping the next generation attached to causes like Palestine, and education. Two years after the Afzaal family murders, still without a conviction, he says the community failed to advocate for its own; the dead and the voiceless depend on those who still have one.

outline.heading: Opening
Series recap
outline.gist: After the verse on Allah standing by the Prophet on the night of Hijrah, he recaps the five categories, his own opinion after ten years here, and why education and mentorship need separate investment in a scattered Western community.

outline.heading: Nusrah: victory from Allah, advocacy from people
outline.gist: From Allah the word means granting victory; from anyone else it means advocating for, supporting and standing by someone. The verse of the Hijrah shows it cannot only mean victory.

outline.heading: Supporting Allah means advocating for His causes
outline.gist: Allah needs no one to grant Him victory, so supporting Him means investing time, wealth, expertise and social or political weight in His causes; then He grants victory.

outline.heading: Al-Anfal: allies must aid those who seek help
outline.gist: The emigrants and those who sheltered them are each other's allies, and believers who ask for help against oppression must be helped unless a treaty prevents it. Muslims here will be asked about this category most, because they can do it.

outline.heading: A Muslim never lets his brother down
outline.gist: The hadith, narrated by many companions in the same words: never turn your back on your brother, and support him whether he is oppressed or an oppressor.

outline.heading: Standing by the oppressor means stopping him
outline.gist: You support an oppressor by holding him back. Whoever watches a believer humiliated and could help but does not will be humiliated by Allah before everyone.

outline.heading: Amr ibn Salim and the Prophet's anger for justice
outline.gist: When Quraysh broke the treaty and massacred Khuza'ah, the Prophet's allies, a survivor came pleading in verse and the Prophet moved an army. He never grew angry for himself, only when justice was violated.

outline.heading: We have voices here, so we are obligated
outline.gist: Most families came from places where an opinion meant mistreatment. While Muslims have a voice here they must use it for the righteous and the oppressed, and stop their own when they oppress.

outline.heading: Not your fight? You will find out it was
outline.gist: Those who thought it was not their problem will be bitterly disappointed on Judgment Day. Oppression is also intellectual, and people now feel the pinch when they cannot uphold their values.

outline.heading: Standing for others makes you vulnerable
outline.gist: Advocacy takes different forms than it did for the Prophet as head of state. Standing for your own rights is easy; standing for someone else's feels like paying for another person's problem.

outline.heading: Ignored oppression comes back to haunt everyone
outline.gist: That mentality is neither healthy nor Islamic; one act of oppression allowed anywhere with a blind eye returns to everyone, as he watched growing up.

outline.heading: The wheel of oppression
outline.gist: Keep quiet while the wheel crushes those around you and it eventually crushes you, and you will wonder why no one stood by you. In Syria a whole village was gassed.

outline.heading: His fellow resident lost his whole village
outline.gist: A friend he shared on-call rooms with in Damascus lost everyone he knew in one day and lost his mind. No one took a stand, just as no one had for neighbouring countries years before.

outline.heading: Interlude
Advocacy through media
outline.gist: The Muslim narrative, what upsets Muslims and makes them feel they do not belong, must reach national and international outlets, or most people never know what Muslims care about.

outline.heading: Lobbying, not political parties
outline.gist: Whoever is elected, nothing changes unless an organized group puts money and votes behind its needs. He does not know how to do it, but the upcoming generation does and should lead with the community's support.

outline.heading: So the oppressed are seen as human
outline.gist: Advocacy is not only for our own rights but so Muslims being starved and killed abroad are at least seen as human and their deaths as a tragedy.

outline.heading: Keep the next generation attached
outline.gist: Children of Palestinians and other oppressed peoples in the subcontinent, China and Africa must still feel they stand for a cause; others are banking on them forgetting within a generation.

outline.heading: Finally, education about the truth
outline.gist: Advocacy depends on accurate information reaching people: what happened and who must be held accountable. He recalls the Afzaal family, who attended his halaqa for years.

outline.heading: The Afzaal family: two years without a conviction
outline.gist: The mother was for two years the only woman at his halaqa; he taught their children. Two years after a man drove into the family on a sidewalk, he is still not convicted.

outline.heading: We do not advocate for ourselves
outline.gist: Had the victim been someone else, the media slogans would have been everywhere. Do not blame others: the community is not organized enough, and whoever turns a blind eye to one person's oppression is next.

outline.heading: The dead depend on our voice
outline.gist: Allowing oppression always returns to haunt, by the way of Allah. The murdered can no longer speak, and many voiceless people worldwide depend on Muslims here to speak for them.

outline.heading: Outro

jh4wN9ldRHQ.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Compeller, Al-Jabbar
jh4wN9ldRHQ.one_line: Al-Jabbar carries two meanings: the One who mends broken hearts again and again, and the One who compels oppressors to His will.
jh4wN9ldRHQ.summary: He presents Al-Jabbar as one of the few names with two meanings, mentioned once in the Quran at the end of Al-Hashr, and addressed especially to the oppressed and inwardly wounded. Linguistically it shares a root with the Arabic word for a cast set on a broken bone; the intensive form means the One who mends what is broken repeatedly. He gives two illustrations of mending. The mother of Musa, forced to cast her infant into the river, felt her heart become empty, and Allah steadied her and returned her son. The Prophet, rejected and stoned at Ta'if, stripped of every kind of support, turned to Allah in his famous complaint of weakness, and moments later was met by Addas, a captive servant who recognised him through the prophet Yunus and kissed his bleeding feet, healing both their hearts. He then turns to the second meaning: Allah also compels tyrants, citing the hadith in which He calls out for the tyrants on the Day of Judgment and a scholar's wonder at anyone who knows Al-Jabbar yet frightens His servants. Everyone meets Al-Jabbar on that day either as the broken who will be mended or the oppressor who will be forced. He asks the audience to seek out broken people and mend them, so that they stand on the mending side of the name.

outline.heading: Each name needs its own approach
outline.gist: The names are not all explained the same way; the variety of angles is meant to touch different parts of life.

outline.heading: A name with two meanings, for the broken
outline.gist: Al-Jabbar appears once, at the end of Al-Hashr, and speaks to anyone oppressed, persecuted or carrying an unseen inner wound.

outline.heading: Jabira, the cast that mends
outline.gist: The root gives the word for a bone cast; the intensive form means the One who mends what is broken over and over, tenderly.

outline.heading: The minbar shook: where are the tyrants
outline.gist: The Prophet recited that Allah will grip the heavens and earth and ask where the tyrants and arrogant are, until the minbar shook beneath him.

outline.heading: The mother of Musa and her empty heart
outline.gist: Told to cast her infant into the river, her heart became void with grief; Allah strengthened her and returned him so her eyes would be cooled.

outline.heading: Ta'if: broken in every way
outline.gist: Seeking only freedom to preach, the Prophet was rejected and stoned until his feet bled, left with no wealth, social, political or religious support.

outline.heading: The hardest day and the dua of complaint
outline.gist: He called that day harder than Uhud, and complained to Allah alone of his weakness, few resources and humiliation.

outline.heading: Addas kisses the bleeding feet
outline.gist: A captive servant brought grapes, recognised him through Yunus, and kissed his feet; Allah mended both the Prophet and the boy, the first believer from outside Arabia.

outline.heading: The second meaning: compelling the oppressor
outline.gist: If you harm and break people, the name applies to you too: Allah forces oppressors to submit to His will and punishment.

outline.heading: Knowing Al-Jabbar yet frightening His servants
outline.gist: A scholar marvelled at one who knows Allah as the Compeller and still intimidates and mistreats His servants.

outline.heading: Meeting Al-Jabbar on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Everyone comes either broken and in need of mending, or as one who wounded others and will be compelled; the two meanings only seem opposite.

outline.heading: Living with the name: mend a broken heart
outline.gist: Look for those who are wounded and fix the break; doctors set bones but hearts are mended by Allah and those He uses, and He will mend yours in turn.

30:50.en: Look, therefore, at the prints of Allah's mercy (in creation): how He quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! He verily is the Quickener of the Dead, and He is Able to do all things

32:21.ar: وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡأَكۡبَرِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
32:21.en: And verily We make them taste the lower punishment before the greater, that haply they may return

Hh8st9VXWb0.speaker: adnan
Hh8st9VXWb0.speaker_note: Ramadan Names of Allah series; addresses 'those of you who are researchers or physicians', his usual style
Hh8st9VXWb0.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Rahman and Al-Raheem
Hh8st9VXWb0.one_line: The names Al-Rahman and Al-Raheem: universal and special mercy, mercy within hardship, and growing compassion as the truest sign of faith.
Hh8st9VXWb0.summary: He explains the two most frequent and inseparable names in the Quran. Divine mercy is compassion that brings about what is truly good for the servant, so like a parent's care it can include hardship. Al-Rahman is mercy for all without exception, while Al-Raheem is special mercy for believers. Mercy is part of Allah's very being, and His mercy outstrips His anger; He sent only one of a hundred mercies to earth, by which a mother shelters her child, keeping ninety-nine for the Day of Judgment, and He is more merciful to us than a mother who would never throw her child into fire. Hardships in this life are mercy too: they wipe sins, raise rank and wake us up, better than being given everything now and facing punishment later. The Prophet was sent as a mercy, and his gentleness held people around him. His central teaching is that the most sensitive indicator of rising faith is growing compassion in heart and behaviour; religiosity that makes you harsher is misunderstood. Mercy is the floor that must remain even toward enemies, in war and in slaughter, while love fluctuates. No one enters Jannah by deeds alone. He closes by urging mercy to all living things and maintaining family ties, which take their name from mercy.

outline.heading: Opening
Two inseparable and most frequent names
outline.gist: Al-Rahman and Al-Raheem occur most in the Quran and are almost never separated.

outline.heading: What divine mercy means
outline.gist: Compassion that brings about the servant's true good, which like a parent's care can include difficulty.

outline.heading: Al-Rahman: mercy for all; Al-Raheem: mercy for believers
outline.gist: The first form is universal with no exceptions; the second is a special mercy channelled to those who believe and follow Him.

outline.heading: Mercy is part of His being and beats His anger
outline.gist: Allah is always merciful but not always angry; He wrote that His mercy overcomes His wrath.

outline.heading: One hundred mercies
outline.gist: One mercy was sent to earth, by which mothers and animals tend their young; ninety-nine are kept for the Day of Judgment, when even Iblis hopes.

outline.heading: More merciful than a mother to her child
outline.gist: Allah has prescribed mercy on Himself and is more merciful to us than a mother who would never throw her child into fire.

outline.heading: Why the basmala names mercy
outline.gist: Of all names, Allah chose to open His book and every act with Al-Rahman and Al-Raheem, repeated in al-Fatihah.

outline.heading: Adam's first words met with mercy
outline.gist: Adam praised Allah and was answered 'may your Lord have mercy on you', the first exchange of creation.

outline.heading: Hardship as a hidden mercy
outline.gist: Everything is good for the believer; trials wipe sins, raise rank and wake us up, better than ease now and loss later.

outline.heading: The Prophet as a mercy to the worlds
outline.gist: His gentleness kept people around him; he was sent only as a mercy.

outline.heading: Compassion: the most sensitive indicator of faith
outline.gist: If your religiosity grows while your mercy shrinks, you are learning Islam wrongly; the closest to Allah was the most merciful.

outline.heading: Mercy in night, day and marriage
outline.gist: Allah made night and day and placed affection and mercy between spouses as signs of His mercy.

outline.heading: Mercy is the floor that never drops
outline.gist: Love fluctuates but mercy must always remain, even toward enemies, in war and when slaughtering animals.

outline.heading: No one enters Jannah by deeds alone
outline.gist: Our worship adds nothing to Allah; entry to Paradise is entirely His mercy, and life reflects it.

outline.heading: Lesser punishments that call us back
outline.gist: Allah sends smaller trials in this life so people return to Him.

outline.heading: The merciful are shown mercy
outline.gist: The first hadith taught to every student: show mercy on earth and the One above shows you mercy; mercy to any living thing is rewarded and never runs out.

outline.heading: Kinship ties named from mercy
outline.gist: Rahim comes from the womb shared by relatives; Allah connects whoever connects it, so Ramadan is the time to mend ties.

outline.heading: Outro

57:20.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱ وَزِينَةࣱ وَتَفَاخُرُۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَتَكَاثُرࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَوۡلَٰدِۖ كَمَثَلِ غَيۡثٍ أَعۡجَبَ ٱلۡكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصۡفَرࣰّ ا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَٰمࣰ اۖ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣱۚ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
57:20.en: Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children; as the likeness of vegetation after rain, whereof the growth is pleasing to the husbandman, but afterward it drieth up and thou seest it turning yellow, then it becometh straw. And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion

57:21.ar: سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:21.en: Race one with another for forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whereof the breadth is as the breadth of the heavens and the earth, which is in store for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. Such is the bounty of Allah, which He bestoweth upon whom He will, and Allah is of Infinite Bounty

57:22.ar: مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن نَّبۡرَأَهَآۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣱ‏
57:22.en: Naught of disaster befalleth in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before we bring it into being - Lo! that is easy for Allah

57:23.ar: لِّكَيۡلَا تَأۡسَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَفۡرَحُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورٍ
57:23.en: That ye grieve not for the sake of that which hath escaped you, nor yet exult because of that which hath been given. Allah loveth not all prideful boasters

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen, and the good things of His providing? Say: Such, on the Day of Resurrection, will be only for those who believed during the life of the world. Thus do we detail Our revelations for people who have knowledge

LrfGIZV5wo4.speaker: adnan
LrfGIZV5wo4.speaker_note: his own continuing Sunday tafseer of Surat al-Hadid
LrfGIZV5wo4.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 6: Verses 20-23
LrfGIZV5wo4.one_line: The five components of the 'low life', the parable of withering crops, racing toward Paradise, and why every calamity is already written.
LrfGIZV5wo4.summary: He begins by arguing that institutions, countries, marriages, mosques and professions fail when mechanics eclipse essence: a mosque is its service and people, bureaucracy is rules that forgot whom they serve, and doctors, teachers and lawyers lose sight of why they work. Both sides are equally important. Verse 20 then defines 'the life of this world' as five instinct-driven pursuits: aimless play, purposeful activity at the wrong time, luxuries, competition for status, and the pursuit of more wealth and children. None is forbidden, but if they fill most of one's life a full revision is needed, because Allah made the world to serve us and created us for more. The parable of rain whose crops delight the farmers, then yellow and crumble, shows how briefly these things last. He advises scheduling leisure, seeking reasonable academic, financial and social stability, and never letting life's distractions pull one from purpose. Verse 21 redirects competition toward forgiveness and a vast Paradise, where competing helps everyone, and stresses that all prophets taught the same essence. Verses 22 and 23 state that every calamity was written before creation; Allah's knowledge does not remove free choice, and its purpose is to keep us from despairing over loss or exulting over gain.

outline.heading: Ask the existential questions early
outline.gist: The cluster sets out life's defining choices; the earlier one, ideally as a teenager, reflects and decides, the better.

outline.heading: Al-Hadid: outer and inner together
outline.gist: Unlike the earlier surahs, any single answer is wrong here: every act needs a measure of mechanics and a measure of essence.

outline.heading: When mechanics eclipse essence
outline.gist: Institutions, nations and marriages that only keep the routine running lose the reason they exist.

outline.heading: A mosque is its people and service
outline.gist: Water and lighting are mechanics; a mosque without education, mentorship and support is empty, while the Prophet's simple, half-roofed mosque produced unmatched light.

outline.heading: Bureaucracy and hollowed-out ideals
outline.gist: Rules meant to serve people become box-ticking, as with the dreaded paperwork day where he grew up; ideals like freedom decay into the freedom to offend and spy.

outline.heading: Prayer reduced to movements
outline.gist: Prayer can shrink to two and a half minutes of motion, yet no qualified scholar would say skip it for dua instead; it means something is missing.

outline.heading: Both are equally important
outline.gist: No argument makes one side more important; fiqh without connection is empty and connection without fiqh worships Allah in ways He did not ask.

outline.heading: Ideas need planning and money
outline.gist: Good ideas die without planning and resources; the Prophet asked the Madinans to pledge their wealth in hardship and ease.

outline.heading: Professionals who forget why they work
outline.gist: Physicians forget they relieve suffering, teachers that they inspire, lawyers that they give a voice to the oppressed.

outline.heading: The world itself is not cursed
outline.gist: The dunya is where prophets lived, books were revealed and we worship; only the 'low life' of bare instinct is criticized.

outline.heading: The life of primitive instinct
outline.gist: All creatures chase survival, food and reproduction; the verse lists five pursuits, none of which is wholly forbidden.

outline.heading: Play: activity with no aim
outline.gist: La'ib is leisure without a higher goal, like a football match whose score changes nothing; permitted, but not a life's purpose.

outline.heading: Diversion: the right thing at the wrong time
outline.gist: Lahw can be useful but is not the priority now, like volunteering or cleaning to avoid studying.

outline.heading: Adornment: wanting a little more luxury
outline.gist: Zinah is the bigger house, newer car and wider screen; no one may forbid it, but recognize it for what it is.

outline.heading: Do not serve what was made to serve you
outline.gist: The world was finely set up for us to use toward a higher purpose; running after it reverses that order and lowers us.

outline.heading: Means, not goal
outline.gist: Wanting a nicer life is fine, but people whose whole talk is earning and spending have turned the tool into the goal.

outline.heading: Rivalry: competing for status
outline.gist: Tafakhur is competing with others for financial, social or political standing, a normal part of working life.

outline.heading: Multiplying wealth and children
outline.gist: Takathur is wanting more for its own sake, not in comparison with anyone: money for financial strength, children for social strength.

outline.heading: Audit your time against the five
outline.gist: Spending months learning a second language while unable to read the Quran shows misprioritizing; if over a fifth of your life falls in these five, revise it.

outline.heading: Allah sees you as worth more
outline.gist: Nothing in these five is impressive; Allah destined you for something more meaningful, and the choice to meet it is yours.

outline.heading: The farmers delighted by the crop
outline.gist: Kuffar here means farmers who cover seeds with soil; the root of covering also explains kufr as covering blessings, and his own village's name.

outline.heading: Green, then yellow, then debris
outline.gist: Worldly pleasures are the brief green stage; only what was used for something beyond them remains.

outline.heading: Schedule your leisure
outline.gist: He treats his leisure time as sacred as his teaching nights, but none of it is why we live.

outline.heading: Only the Prophet needed none of it
outline.gist: He sought no fun, luxury, rivalry or increase and was still the happiest of people; the rest of us need these things in moderation.

outline.heading: Reach stability by thirty
outline.gist: Be satisfied academically by about thirty and reach some financial and social stability; imams without it, often without pensions, carry a real lack.

outline.heading: Life's distractions pull people away
outline.gist: Many who were focused drift after graduating, marrying and having children, until they visit the mosque monthly; that is exactly what to guard against.

outline.heading: Punishment, forgiveness and passing enjoyment
outline.gist: The Hereafter holds both severe punishment and forgiveness with His pleasure; the world is an enjoyable illusion, merely rented, even our bones.

outline.heading: Race toward a garden as vast as the heavens
outline.gist: Instead of rivalry for status, race each other to forgiveness and a Paradise whose expanse, like the universe, has no visible end.

outline.heading: Belief in Allah and all His messengers
outline.gist: Naming all the messengers means believing in Allah as He taught every prophet; their rulings differed but the essence was identical.

outline.heading: Competition for the Hereafter is not zero-sum
outline.gist: Worldly races have one winner; in this race there are infinite places, competing motivates others, and Allah may raise the other to the same rank.

outline.heading: No abrogation in matters of faith
outline.gist: Abrogation touches rulings like timings and food, never the essence of who Allah is and our purpose.

outline.heading: His bounty to whom He wills and who wants it
outline.gist: The wording allows both readings at once: He offers it to whom He wills, and to those who truly want it over the low life.

outline.heading: The rich are not happy; love of Allah lasts
outline.gist: Yachts and parties bring momentary highs that the elderly cannot relive, while a heart full of Allah's love stays joyful to its last moment.

outline.heading: Interlude
Every calamity written before creation
outline.gist: No misfortune on earth or in ourselves occurs without being recorded before life itself existed.

outline.heading: A question that split the early sects
outline.gist: Qadar is among his most frequent questions and divided theological groups in Islam's first centuries, though the Quran makes it clear.

outline.heading: Of course He knows
outline.gist: It is effortless for Allah; a god who did not know what happens in His universe would not be worthy of worship.

outline.heading: Knowing is not causing
outline.gist: Knowing chickens lay eggs does not make them lay; and there is no 'future' for Allah, since time is His creation and He is the First and the Last.

outline.heading: Our choices are real
outline.gist: We can do anything right now, which Allah knew and recorded; arguing philosophy beyond our grasp has only caused division.

outline.heading: So you neither despair nor exult
outline.gist: The purpose of knowing it was written is to keep us from over-grieving losses or becoming vain over blessings, since Allah does not love the boastful.

35:41.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمۡسِكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ أَن تَزُولَاۚ وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَهُمَا مِنۡ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
35:41.en: Lo! Allah graspeth the heavens and the earth that they deviate not, and if they were to deviate there is not one that could grasp them after Him. Lo! He is ever Clement, Forgiving

2:263.ar: ۞قَوۡلࣱ مَّعۡرُوفࣱ وَمَغۡفِرَةٌ خَيۡرࣱ مِّن صَدَقَةࣲ يَتۡبَعُهَآ أَذࣰ ىۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمࣱ‏
2:263.en: A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement

9:114.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱسۡتِغۡفَارُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوۡعِدَةࣲ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥٓ أَنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ لِّلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُۚ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
9:114.en: The prayer of Abraham for the forgiveness of his father was only because of a promise he had promised him, but when it had become clear unto him that he (his father) was an enemy to Allah he (Abraham) disowned him. Lo! Abraham was soft of heart, long-suffering

37:101.en: So We gave him tidings of a gentle son

11:87.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
11:87.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! Doth thy way of prayer command thee that we should forsake that which our fathers (used to) worship, or that we (should leave off) doing what we will with our own property. Lo! thou art the mild, the guide to right behaviour

3:134.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلۡكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
3:134.en: Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good

42:43.ar: وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
42:43.en: And verily whoso is patient and forgiveth - lo! that, verily, is (of) the steadfast heart of things

7:199.ar: خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.en: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant

I5KYsr1vvUE.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The Forbearing, Al-Halim
I5KYsr1vvUE.one_line: Al-Halim: Allah does not rush to punish despite our sins, and the Prophet's forbearance under provocation shows how we should live it.
I5KYsr1vvUE.summary: He explains Al-Halim, which appears eleven times in the Quran, as the One who does not hurry to punish servants who deserve it, giving them time to put things right. He reads meaning from the names it is paired with: forgiving, all-knowing, free of need and appreciative. He then argues that sabr and hilm are different: sabr is perseverance against hardship, like climbing a mountain in a storm, while hilm is not reacting when provoked, which is why he is inclined to think As-Sabur is not a name of Allah. He cites Allah holding the heavens and earth from collapse despite human oppression, the verse preferring a kind word to charity followed by insult, prophets described as forbearing, and the verses on suppressing anger and overlooking the ignorant. Hadith and seerah examples follow: do not get angry, the praise of Ashajj of Abd al-Qays, the man who held a sword to the sleeping Prophet and was spared, the Prophet's prayer for his people after his wounds at Uhud, and the rabbi who lent money and provoked him only to find that his patience grew with every insult. He asks people to show forbearance at home with spouses and children during a time of being stuck indoors, remembering that Allah gives us one chance after another.

outline.heading: Al-Halim in the Quran and its paired names
outline.gist: The name appears eleven times, most often paired with Al-Ghafur, then Al-Alim, Al-Ghani and Ash-Shakur.

outline.heading: Paired with forgiveness: not hurrying to punish
outline.gist: Hilm means not rushing to punish those who deserve it, giving them time to correct; paired with forgiveness it balances both ideas.

outline.heading: Paired with knowledge, self-sufficiency and appreciation
outline.gist: He knows all our sins yet waits; He needs no one yet does not mistreat; and He rewards small deeds generously.

outline.heading: Sabr and hilm are not the same
outline.gist: Sabr is perseverance against hardship, hilm is not reacting when provoked; since Allah never needs to persevere, he holds As-Sabur is not one of His names.

outline.heading: Holding the heavens and earth from collapse
outline.gist: Despite all the world's oppression Allah keeps the heavens and earth from falling apart because He is forbearing.

outline.heading: A kind word is better than charity followed by hurt
outline.gist: Allah needs no charity and is forbearing toward those who give and then remind people of it.

outline.heading: Forbearing prophets
outline.gist: Ibrahim, the son promised to him and Shu'ayb are described with hilm, even by mockers who meant it as an insult.

outline.heading: Suppressing anger and forgiving
outline.gist: For believers in general the Quran praises those who restrain anger, pardon and persevere when they feel the urge to react.

outline.heading: Take what is good and overlook the ignorant
outline.gist: People bring both good and bad; take the best of their conduct, encourage good and turn away from ignorance.

outline.heading: Do not get angry
outline.gist: The man who asked for advice was told three times not to let anger overcome him, the best advice anyone can receive.

outline.heading: Ashajj of Abd al-Qays
outline.gist: The Prophet praised the tribal leader for two traits Allah loves, deliberateness and forbearance, which were part of his nature.

outline.heading: The sword at the sleeping Prophet's throat
outline.gist: A man asked who would save him now; the sword fell, the Prophet held it and still spared him after he refused Islam, to the companions' awe.

outline.heading: Wounds at Uhud and a prayer for his people
outline.gist: Bleeding with helmet links in his cheek and a broken tooth, he was asked to curse the enemy and instead asked Allah to forgive his people who did not know.

outline.heading: The rabbi's loan and his provocation
outline.gist: A rabbi who found every sign but one lent money for a year, returned in days demanding it and insulted the Prophet until Umar could not bear it.

outline.heading: The more he was provoked, the more patient he became
outline.gist: The Prophet told Umar to urge both sides to better conduct; the man revealed he was testing the last sign, forbearance that grows with provocation.

outline.heading: Living the name: forbearance at home
outline.gist: Be forbearing with spouse and children while stuck at home, especially mothers who cannot leave, remembering Allah gives chance after chance.

outline.heading: Outro
